props.alt: Hoist drive with numbered parts: 1 the motor, 2 a planetary stage whose held member is still to choose, 3 the drum, 4 the load hanging from the rope. An arrow shows the lifting direction.

props.markdown:
A customer orders a hoist drive. The motor (1) turns at **1,450 rpm**. The drum (3) must turn at **about 360 rpm**, in the **same direction** as the motor, to lift the 2-tonne load (4).

You have one planetary stage (2): a **24-tooth sun** and a **72-tooth ring**. The test bench will measure the drum before the drive ships.

props.prompt: **Which configuration do you send to the test bench?**

options.label: Hold the ring, drive the sun, take the drum off the carrier
Hold the sun, drive the ring, take the drum off the carrier
Hold the carrier, drive the sun, take the drum off the ring

props.alt: Bench gauge: the drum turns at 363 rpm, inside the 340 to 380 rpm target band, in the lifting direction. Result accepted.

props.title: Within target
props.markdown: $24 \times 1450 + 72 \times 0 = 96\,n_c$, so the drum turns at **363 rpm**, in the same direction as the motor. The 4 : 1 reduction also multiplies the motor torque by about four, minus the losses.

props.alt: Bench gauge: the drum turns at 1,088 rpm, far above the 340 to 380 rpm target band, in the lifting direction. Result rejected.

props.title: Three times too fast
props.markdown:
$72 \times 1450 = 96\,n_c$ gives **1,088 rpm**. Holding the sun gives the mildest reduction (1.33 : 1): the load would rise three times faster than specified, with a third of the torque.

To reach 360 rpm you need the strongest reduction: hold the **ring**, drive the **sun**, take the output from the **carrier** (4 : 1).

props.alt: Bench gauge: the drum turns at 483 rpm, above the 340 to 380 rpm target band, and in the lowering direction. Result rejected.

props.title: The drum turns the wrong way
props.markdown:
With the carrier held, $24 \times 1450 + 72\,n_r = 0$ gives $n_r = -483$ rpm: pressing LIFT lowers the load, and too fast.

To lift at 360 rpm, hold the **ring**, drive the **sun** and take the output from the **carrier** (4 : 1, same direction).
